summary: THREE CONFIRMED SCHEMA DRIFTS that make parts of the news feed silently empty, all found by applying the Wave 35 Objective-3 lesson (absence of findings is not evidence) to discover's own surface. None produces a tsc diagnostic, a test failure, or a CodeQL alert. All three are database-owned fixes; discover could not apply them and did NOT paper over them by deleting the offending columns. A fourth item, `artist_music`'s trust columns, is only a CONTRACT-staleness problem and needs no action. (1) `artist_blog_posts.format` — the column is created ONLY by supabase/migration-archive/pre-reconciliation-local-only-2026-08-20/20260717220000_press_content_formats.sql, which is ARCHIVED and not in the active chain. lib/news/feed-service.ts:376-397 selects it and filters `.in('format', ['article','blog'])` on it, so PostgREST 400s and the ENTIRE blog section of the news feed is empty. Live code depends on it, so the fix is to port that migration back, not to remove the select. (2) `music_tracks.{origin_status,certification_status,certification_level,certification_public_id}` — `music_tracks` is a VIEW whose projection (supabase/migrations/20260711165607_native_music_player_hardening.sql:118-158) does not include those four columns; they were added to the base TABLE afterwards at supabase/migrations/20260910140000_artist_music_trust_columns.sql:12-15, and a base-table column does not appear in an existing view. The select 400s and the entire music section of the news feed is empty. Fix: an additive `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public.music_tracks` that adds the four columns. (3) `user_news_preferences` and `user_news_subscriptions` — created by NO migration anywhere under supabase/. The code's `catch { // Table may not exist yet in early rollout }` comment is therefore not describing a temporary state: the news personalization signal (subscribed topics, subscribed sources) is PERMANENTLY empty. Fix: either author the two tables additively, or delete the dead reads.

Item 1: `artist_blog_posts` is created in the active chain at supabase/migrations/20260702210503_account_aware_blog_publishing.sql:9-33 and extended at :54-61. Neither adds `format`, and `rg -n 'artist_blog_posts' supabase/migrations/*.sql | rg -i format` returns nothing. `format`, `distribution`, `subtitle`, `boilerplate` and `embargo_until` all come from the ARCHIVED 20260717220000_press_content_formats.sql. lib/database.types.ts `artist_blog_posts.Row` has 25 columns and none of them is `format`.

Its explicit projection does not include the four trust columns, and the only migration that adds them targets `public.artist_music`, not the view. `drop view if exists public.music_tracks cascade; create view ...` in that migration is the shape a redefinition must follow.
Item 3: `rg -ln 'user_news_preferences|user_news_subscriptions' supabase/migrations/*.sql` and the same search over all of `supabase/` both return nothing. No migration creates either table.

Discovered and DISCARDED a proposed in-file 'fix': removing `format` from the select. It would have made the blog section non-empty, but it deletes a column the press lane owns and that __tests__/press/press-formats-and-news.test.ts:30 asserts on, and it would convert a visible schema regression into an invisible one. Reverted. discover does not get to decide whether press formats are still a product requirement.

Removed the dead 'legacy' retry that sat in fetchBlogCandidates. It re-selected `format` and so could never succeed; the only observable difference is that the PostgREST error is now logged once instead of twice.

Made every failure LOUD rather than silent, which is the part discover could do without touching the schema: fetchBlogCandidates and fetchMusicCandidates now destructure `error`, log `[News feed] ... query failed: <message>`, and return []. Previously both discarded `error` entirely.

All three are `planned` / manual-apply-pending under CP-051 and NOTHING was applied to any environment.

THE HANDOFF'S COMPLETION CONDITION IS MET, AND BY A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT THAN IT ASKED FOR. It asked that music_tracks be added to supabase/tests/db008_view_relation_list.txt asserting the four trust columns. The list ALREADY contained music_tracks, so no list change was needed; instead `npm run check:db008-harness` now measures the fix with the repository's existing view-column replay, which extracts the migration's CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW byte-verbatim from the chain and lets a real PostgreSQL 16.15 resolve the SELECT list: music_tracks resolved=38, declared=34, VIEW-ONLY=origin_status,certification_status,certification_level,certification_public_id, TOTAL contractOnlyColumns=0. That is the independent confirmation the handoff wanted, and it required no new harness file — which also kept DB-019 inside its literal three-filename working set.

ONE FACT IN THE HANDOFF WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT. It records the live music_tracks projection as having 36 columns. It has 34, measured by letting PostgreSQL resolve the chain view's own SELECT list. The four trust columns bring it to 38, not 40. The migration's post-condition asserts 38 and names all 34 pre-existing columns individually, so a count copied from the handoff would have reported every healthy target as broken.

ONE ITEM THE HANDOFF DID NOT NAME WAS FOUND WHILE AUTHORING AND IS ROUTED, NOT ABSORBED: public.press_release_shares is a SIXTH gap of the identical class (archived 20260717221000, absent from the chain AND the contract, live consumers), and its absence makes canAccessPressRelease return allowed:false for every NON-owner, so the press-release share and PDF-download feature 403s for every shared recipient. DB-019's press migration restores the columns getPressReleaseById reads, so that function now gets FURTHER before it returns false. Routed to the artist lane as HF-DB-019-PRESS-RELEASE-SHARES-CHAIN-SURFACE.
